transcript_evidence.claim: On the Q2 2026 earnings call, management said net revenue rose 17% to $11.2 billion and EPS rose 20%, calling it Visa’s strongest net revenue growth since 2022 and, excluding unusual comparison periods, since 2013.

transcript_evidence.claim: Management reported payments volume of $3.7 trillion, up 9% constant-currency, and processed transactions of 66 billion, up 9%.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: CEO Ryan McInerney framed Visa as the “leading hyperscaler of payments globally” and said its Visa as a Service stack should drive future growth across consumer, commercial, money movement, AI/agentic commerce, stablecoins/blockchain, and value-added services.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management presented multiple strategic growth vectors for Visa’s platform.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Our business has incredible momentum. Visa has become the leading hyperscaler of payments globally. Our strategy and Visa as a Service stack will help us drive future growth in four important ways. One, we are winning in consumer payments, commercial payments, and money movement. Our investments and innovations are paying off in a meaningful way and will continue to drive growth.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management said AI and agentic commerce can expand Visa’s addressable market and accelerate long-term growth.
transcript_evidence.summary: Visa positioned AI and agentic commerce as a long-term growth opportunity.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Two, AI and agentic commerce will expand our addressable market and our efforts will accelerate Visa's long-term growth.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management described stablecoins and blockchain as significant opportunities and positioned Visa as an interoperability layer between new infrastructure and real-world user solutions.

transcript_evidence.excerpt: Three, stablecoins and blockchain are significant opportunities, we've established Visa's role as a key interoperability layer between this powerful infrastructure and real-world solutions for users.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Value-added services represented 30% of Visa net revenue and were growing more than 25% in constant dollars, according to management.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management highlighted VAS as a large and fast-growing part of Visa revenue.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Four, value-added services is an even bigger opportunity and has demonstrated its value as a key driver of our growth, now representing 30% of our net revenue, growing at 25%+ in constant $.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Visa is pursuing fintech, wallet, and app partnerships, including TikTok in the U.K. and PayPay in Japan, to capture both carded and non-carded payments.
